input.description: Refillable, concentrated cleaning products. Skip the single-use plastic bottles. Works as well as the big brands. We want to show up where people who already care about sustainability are checking out.

brief.statusReason: The business clearly offers eco-friendly household cleaning products aimed at sustainability-minded shoppers.
brief.productSummary: Refillable and concentrated household cleaning products sold to eco-conscious consumers at a mid-tier price level.
assumptions: Assumed mid-tier pricing typical for eco-friendly concentrated cleaning refills.
Assumed both one-time purchases and refill subscriptions may be offered as purchase model was not specified.

persona.name: The Sustainability Buyer
persona.description: Makes purchase decisions based on environmental and ethical footprint. Researches supply chains. Will pay more for genuinely sustainable options and is skeptical of greenwashing.

persona.name: The Busy Parent
persona.description: Dual-income household with kids. Time-poor, convenience-motivated. Buys in bulk, loves subscriptions, trusts brands that have been recommended by other parents.

persona.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
persona.description: Budget-aware but not low-end. Looks for deals, reads reviews, comparison shops. Responds well to bundles, first-order discounts, and clear value articulation.

persona.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
persona.description: Highly visual, identity-expressive buyer. Discovers through TikTok and Instagram. Cares about brand voice, packaging, and whether the brand stands for something.

persona.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
persona.description: Works out 4+ times a week, follows fitness creators, buys performance apparel and supplements. Brand-loyal to things that perform. Identity-adjacent purchasing.

persona.name: The Wellness Optimizer
persona.description: Tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts. Treats her body like a system to optimize. Willing to pay premiums for evidence-backed products.

persona.name: The Pet Parent
persona.description: Treats their pet as a family member. Reads ingredient labels on pet food. Will pay a premium for health and quality. Often owns multiple pets.

persona.name: The Affluent Classic
persona.description: Established career or retired, disposable income, values quality and longevity over trends. Shops less frequently but at higher AOVs. Loyal to brands she trusts.

persona.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
persona.description: Urban, mid-to-high income, values speed and frictionlessness. Default to what's easy. Heavy subscription user. Low brand loyalty if another option is just as convenient.

persona.name: The Gifter
persona.description: Not a persistent persona so much as a mode: any shopper within 30 days of a gifting holiday or life event. Higher AOV, looking for 'impressive-looking' purchases. Very responsive to gift-wrap and gifting messaging.

publisher.name: Pantrygood
publisher.notes: Values-driven shoppers. Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Sustainability Buyer, The Busy Parent, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publishers.rationale: Pantrygood's high-income, values-driven customer base actively seeks out clean ingredients and sustainable household essentials, making this an ideal match for your refillable cleaning line.
publishers.concern: Subscription-oriented shoppers may expect seamless refill recurring delivery integrations.

publisher.name: Swiftcart
publisher.notes: High-frequency purchasers. Late-night traffic spike. Impulse-friendly.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Sustainability Buyer, The Busy Parent, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publishers.rationale: While Swiftcart reaches high-frequency household buyers, its impulse-driven and late-night convenience traffic does not align with the intentionality needed to adopt refillable cleaning systems.
publishers.concern: Impulse shoppers prioritize instant single-use convenience over concentrated refill routines.

publisher.name: Kitchenly
publisher.notes: Family and couples households. Convenience-motivated but food-interested.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Busy Parent, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publishers.rationale: Kitchenly reaches family and couple households focused on kitchen and home maintenance, offering strong contextual relevance for cleaning products.
publishers.concern: Audience interest is primarily meal-focused, requiring clean-up messaging to bridge the gap.

publisher.name: Stride & Stem
publisher.notes: Professional women. Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Sustainability Buyer, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publishers.rationale: Although these professional women care about sustainability and product care, their primary purchase mindset on this platform is centered strictly on footwear and fashion.
publishers.concern: Low contextual relevance for household cleaning supplies may dampen click-through and conversion.

publisher.name: Cloudfoot
publisher.notes: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging.

publishers.rationale: While these urban professionals appreciate both sustainability and performance messaging, their intent on Cloudfoot is focused on activewear rather than domestic supplies.
publishers.concern: The footwear catalog creates a significant category disconnect for household cleaners.

publisher.name: Hearthstone Goods
publisher.notes: Sustainability-motivated kitchen buyers. Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase.

publisher.name: Pawline
publisher.notes: Subscription-heavy. Owners are health-conscious about pets, responsive to premium positioning.

publisher.name: Ruffco
publisher.notes: Largest pet audience in the catalog. Broad demographics, repeat-purchase behavior.

publisher.name: Northbed
publisher.notes: Design-conscious urban/suburban buyers. High cross-sell with home and wellness.

publisher.name: Velvetline
publisher.notes: Gen Z and younger millennial. Minimalist aesthetic, identity-driven purchasing.

publisher.name: Strandlab
publisher.notes: Personalization-motivated audience. Quiz-based onboarding elsewhere.

publisher.name: Movewell
publisher.notes: Fitness-engaged shoppers. Strong crossover with wellness and beauty.

publisher.name: Marlowe & Co.
publisher.notes: Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV. Responds to quality messaging.

publisher.name: Linden Park
publisher.notes: Highest-AOV apparel publisher in the catalog. Conservative brand sensibility.

publisher.name: Everbody
publisher.notes: Inclusive sizing across the full range. Audience values representation and fit-focused messaging.

publisher.name: Studiogrid
publisher.notes: Appointment-based booking. Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Heartfoot
publisher.notes: Strong gifting season uplift (Nov-Dec). Audience responds to social-good messaging.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Daily Form
publisher.notes: Science-forward wellness. Audience skeptical of unsubstantiated health claims.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Tailcrate
publisher.notes: Millennials treating dogs as family. Fun, playful brand voice converts best.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.notes: Health-curious but indulgence-seeking. Strong overlap with wellness and premium grocery.

plan.reviewNote: Pantry and kitchen grocery platforms offer the strongest immediate intent for household cleaning concentrates, while apparel partners provide demographic value alignment but suffer from category mismatch.

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
No price given: used the spend-weighted publisher AOV (~$68) as order value.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed mid-tier pricing typical for eco-friendly concentrated cleaning refills.
Assumed both one-time purchases and refill subscriptions may be offered as purchase model was not specified.

output.understanding: The advertiser offers sustainable, concentrated, refillable cleaning products designed to eliminate single-use plastic while matching legacy brand performance, targeting eco-conscious home care shoppers.

publishers.rationale: Pantrygood's audience consists of values-driven shoppers focused on organic goods, clean ingredients, and sustainability, making it the highest-affinity grocery platform for sustainable home cleaning.
Hearthstone Goods attracts sustainability-focused consumers actively seeking non-toxic kitchen and home essentials with high purchasing intent.
Northbed reaches design- and wellness-conscious homeowners and renters looking to maintain their living spaces, offering strong contextual crossover for home cleaning goods.

excluded.reason: Audience skews toward late-night impulse and convenience purchases rather than mission-driven, eco-conscious household cleaning.
Primarily focused on activewear and fitness apparel with limited crossover intent for household cleaning solutions.
Service- and appointment-based wellness booking platform without direct contextual alignment to physical home cleaning goods.
Apparel-focused publisher catering to older women looking for workwear and classic fashion rather than eco-cleaning essentials.
High-end classic apparel platform with minimal context or relevance to sustainable household consumables.
Focus is strictly on inclusive sizing apparel and intimates, lacking relevance to cleaning and home maintenance.
Audience shopping behavior is exclusively tailored to pet supplies, treats, and food.
Broad mass-market pet platform without a dedicated environmental or home sustainability focus.
Apparel and gifting platform specializing in basic wear and socks rather than household surface care.
Audience seeks science-backed personal ingestible supplements and vitamins rather than surface cleaning products.
Gen Z and millennial beauty and skincare community with minimal intent for household cleaning supplies.
While grocery and home-centric, meal-kit shoppers prioritize quick food prep over specialized zero-waste cleaning solutions.
Sustainable apparel and footwear audience offers conceptual eco-alignment but lacks immediate home care purchase context.
Focus on sustainable activewear and footwear does not provide natural context for home cleaning products.
Millennial pet toy and treat subscription marketplace without relevance to non-pet cleaning supplies.
Dedicated haircare customization platform with zero overlap with household surface cleaners.
Beverage and gut-health marketplace with purchase occasions focused entirely on ingestible wellness.
